notes: IFRS (EU-endorsed) throughout FY2007-FY2025: LVMH has reported under IFRS since 2005, so there is no local-GAAP year and no standard change inside the window.

operatingIncome = the "Operating profit" line of the consolidated income statement (résultat opérationnel, i.e. after other non-recurring operating income and expenses). LVMH's headline KPI is "Profit from recurring operations" (résultat opérationnel courant), which is higher: 2025 17,755; 2024 19,571; 2023 22,802; 2022 21,055; 2021 17,151; 2020 8,305; 2019 11,504; 2018 10,003; 2017 8,293; 2016 7,026; 2015 6,605; 2014 5,715; 2013 6,017; 2012 5,924; 2011 5,263; 2010 4,321; 2009 3,352; 2008 3,628; 2007 3,555 (EUR millions). Yahoo's operatingIncome is the recurring figure.

capex = "Acquisitions of intangible assets and property, plant and equipment" as published by LVMH in the business review (FY2018-FY2025), stored negative. That published figure is identical to the "net cash used in purchases of fixed assets" line of the operating-investments note (e.g. FY2018: 2,990), so the same line is used for FY2007-FY2017. It is net of the change in fixed-asset payables and of assets acquired under finance leases, hence slightly below gross capital expenditure.

totalDebt = long-term borrowings + short-term borrowings ("gross borrowings") from the consolidated balance sheet; lease liabilities (IFRS 16, from 2019) and purchase commitments for minority interests' shares are excluded.

cashAndEquivalents = "Cash and cash equivalents" on the balance sheet. The cash-flow statement's closing figure is lower because it is net of bank overdrafts (FY2025: 8,359 vs 8,794; FY2018: 4,413 vs 4,610; FY2008: 718 vs 1,013).
netIncome and totalEquity are the amounts attributable to owners of the parent ("Net profit, Group share" / "Equity, Group share").

Restatements (latest published figure used, restated=true): FY2007 balance sheet restated in the FY2008 document for the offsetting of income tax assets and liabilities against advance tax payments; FY2008 restated in the FY2010 document for the IAS 38 amendment (total assets 31,577 -> 31,483; equity 12,897 -> 12,804); FY2011 restated in the FY2013 document for amended IAS 19 (equity 22,451 -> 22,371); FY2012 restated in the FY2014 document for IFRS 11 (total assets 49,930 -> 49,850); FY2013 restated in the FY2014/FY2015 documents for IFRS 11 and the Loro Piana purchase price allocation; FY2016 and FY2017 restated in the FY2018 document for IFRS 9 and the Christian Dior Couture purchase price allocation (FY2017 net profit 5,129 -> 5,365, diluted EPS 10.18 -> 10.64; FY2016 net profit 3,981 -> 4,066).

Budget/scope breaks to keep in mind: FY2018 was explicitly NOT restated for IFRS 16 (footnote in the 2020 URD), so its balance sheet carries no right-of-use assets or lease liabilities, while FY2019 onwards do (FY2020 long-term borrowings jump by 9 billion euros for that reason, and cash rises to 19,963 as debt was pre-funded). FY2014 net profit (5,648) includes 2,677 million euros (5.34 euros per share) from the distribution in kind of the Hermès shares, so it is not comparable with neighbouring years.

Revenue for FY2012 and FY2013 is the reclassified figure published from the FY2014 document onwards (27,970 and 29,016, versus 28,103 and 29,149 as first reported) - a 133 million euro reclassification in both years.

FY2007-FY2017 figures come from LVMH's "Documents financiers / Financial documents" (condensed consolidated statements with three-year comparatives). LVMH no longer serves those PDFs from lvmh.com (the old r.lvmh-static.com links now redirect to the homepage), so the Internet Archive copies of the original files are cited; each cited archive URL was opened and its byte size matches the file read. FY2018-FY2025 come from the Universal Registration Documents hosted on lvmh.com. Each year is taken from the latest document that reports it as a comparative: FY2007 from FY2008, FY2008 from FY2010, FY2009 from FY2011, FY2010 from FY2012, FY2011 from FY2013, FY2012 from FY2014, FY2013-FY2014 from FY2015, FY2015 from FY2017, FY2016-FY2017 from FY2018, FY2018-FY2019 from the 2020 URD, FY2020-FY2021 from the 2022 URD, FY2022 from the 2022 URD, FY2023 from the 2024 URD, FY2024-FY2025 from the 2025 URD.

dividendPerShare = gross dividend per share for the fiscal year as published in the group's "Data per share"/highlights page (FY2007-FY2008: amount paid during the period; FY2025: amount proposed to the AGM). FY2020 2.00 interim + 4.00 final = 6.00; FY2019 2.20 + 2.60 = 4.80; FY2018 2.00 + 4.00 = 6.00 - the FY2019 total is lower only because its final dividend was 2.60 rather than 4.00.

sharesOutstanding = number of shares in issue at 31 December per the statement of changes in equity (treasury shares held remain in issue). The 2011 jump from 490,642,232 to 507,815,624 is the 18,037,011 shares issued for Bulgari plus option exercises; later decreases are share retirements (LVMH cancels the shares it buys back).

employees = total headcount at 31 December (permanent + fixed-term contracts) from the group's "Total workforce as of December 31" table: FY2018 156,088; FY2019 163,309; FY2020 150,479; FY2021 175,647; FY2022 196,006; FY2023 213,268; FY2024 215,637. FY2025 211,552 excludes apprenticeships and vocational training contracts (all-in workforce 213,932), so FY2025 is slightly narrower in scope than FY2023-FY2024. The FY2007-FY2017 Financial Documents publish no headcount at all, hence null.

Cross-check against docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json (USD, divided by the implied average rate): revenue and net income agree to the million for FY2022-FY2025 (implied rates 1.0517 / 1.0849 / 1.0802 / 1.1323), e.g. FY2025 revenue 91,496.0m USD / 1.1323 = 80,807m EUR and net income 12,316.9m USD / 1.1323 = 10,878m EUR; FY2022 83,278.6 / 1.0517 = 79,184 and 14,812.5 / 1.0517 = 14,084. Yahoo's operatingIncome is "Profit from recurring operations", not the "Operating profit" stored here (FY2025 17,755 vs 17,099), and its dilutedEPS for FY2025 is a USD-converted 24.74 (21.85 EUR).

FY2007's balance sheet is as published in the FY2008 document, which restated it only for income-tax offsetting. The IAS 38 amendment adopted in 2010 applied retrospectively to 1 January 2007, but LVMH presented only the restated FY2008 comparative, so an IAS 38-consistent FY2007 balance sheet was never published; treat FY2007 totalAssets/totalEquity as the pre-amendment figures.
